Samuel's sons accepted bribes (1 Sam 8:3), and Isaiah condemns Jerusalem's rulers as 'lovers of bribes' (Isa 1:23). The word can extend to political inducements between kings (1 Kgs 15:19). Proverbs observes with realism that 'a bribe is a charm stone in the eyes of its owner' (Prov 17:8). Spanish 'soborno' and French 'bribe' reflect its judicial core."

Prophets denounce bribe-takers (Isa 1:23; Mic 3:11). Wisdom observes its power as a 'charm stone' (Prov 17:8) while condemning it (Prov 17:23). Also covers political payments between kings (1 Kgs 15:19).
    Existing Spanish translations: Soborno, Y-soborno, el-soborno, por-soborno, soborno, y-soborno
